title: Graphing a Reflected and Vertically Shifted Two-Thirds Power Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = 1 - x^(2/3) by identifying its parent function, transformations, cusp, domain, range, and intercepts.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = x^{2/3} \text{ reflected across x-axis and shifted up } 1;\quad \text{Cusp: } (0, 1),\quad \text{Domain: } (-\infty, \infty),\quad \text{Range: } (-\infty, 1],\quad \text{x-intercepts: } (\pm 1, 0)

steps.title: Identify the Transformations from y = x^(2/3)
steps.explanation: Start with the even parent curve y = x^(2/3), reflect it across the x-axis to get y = -x^(2/3) (opening downward), and shift it up 1 unit to get y = 1 - x^(2/3).
steps.why: Multiplying by -1 reflects across the x-axis, and adding 1 shifts vertically upward by 1.

steps.title: Find the Cusp, Domain, Range, and Symmetry
steps.explanation: Since x^(2/3) >= 0 for all real x, we have 1 - x^(2/3) <= 1, with an upward-pointing cusp at (0, 1) and even symmetry across the y-axis.
steps.why: Negating a non-negative function with minimum 0 creates a function with maximum 0, which shifts to maximum 1.

steps.title: Determine the Intercepts
steps.explanation: The curve peaks at the y-intercept (0, 1) and descends symmetrically on both sides through the x-intercepts (-1, 0) and (1, 0) and through (-8, -3) and (8, -3).
